propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark calls author() 6,000 times, executing git config user.name lookup via subprocess once per envelope, consuming 47.79s cumulatively.
The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging once per new CREATE ticket (3,000 times) rather than once per batch, performing 375,876 redundant staging-owner checks and consuming 15.94s.
Import-scoped contextvar author caching keyed by fallback reduces git config reads to exactly one per import while preserving live lookup behavior for interactive/direct writes.

Deferring stale-staging sweep until the first new-ticket item in each bounded batch reduces sweeps from 3,000 to approximately 12 (one per CREATE chunk) without changing crash-resume, rollback, or atomic publish behavior.
The optimization preserves the locked N=3000 contract: 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, exactly 24 commits, >=10x commit-count reduction, and all durability/safety semantics.

Controlled A/B profiling on identical-state harness confirmed -60.8s (78.8% reduction) by replacing only the two redundant mechanisms while preserving event bytes, author attribution fallback parity, and logical state.
